is_anopheles.evidence: The study was conducted on Anopheles funestus (both field F1 progeny and laboratory strains; page 3, 'Mosquito collection and rearing').

reports_target_markers.evidence: Genotyped the GSTe2 L119F marker in field-collected An. funestus (page 5, 'Genotyping of L119F-GSTe2 mutation in field-collected strain') and CYP6P9a_R in lab crosses (page 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts for L119F-GSTe2 in field An. funestus are provided on page 7: among 360 blood-fed mosquitoes, 24 RR, 103 RS, 233 SS; among 300 unfed mosquitoes, 15 RR, 62 RS, 189 SS. Page 9 also reports genotype counts for probing/feeding duration (7 RR, 40 RS, 67 SS out of 114 successfully genotyped).

african_field_population.evidence: Field mosquitoes were F1 adults reared from wild-caught indoor-resting females (F0) collected in Mibellon, Cameroon (page 3, 'Mosquito collection and rearing').

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical research study assessing the effect of metabolic resistance markers on blood-feeding parameters.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections occurred in 'Mibellon (6ɖ46’N, 11⁰ 70’E), a village located in a rural area of the savanna-forest region in Cameroon' (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Although specific collection months/years are not explicitly stated in the text, national ethics clearance was granted in April 2018 (Nɖ2018/04/1000/CE/CNERSH/SP) and the manuscript was received in March 2020, constraining the collection window to ≤3 years (2018–2020).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Mosquitoes were newly collected and reared at the CRID insectary in Yaound�e for this specific blood-feeding experimental trial.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and results are presented in the main text and figures; S1 Table contains only qPCR primer sequences.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the effect of pyrethroid metabolic resistance markers on blood feeding in Anopheles funestus. F1 progeny from field-caught An. funestus from Mibellon, Cameroon were genotyped for GSTe2 L119F, reporting extractable genotype counts for blood-fed (24 RR, 103 RS, 233 SS) and unfed (15 RR, 62 RS, 189 SS) mosquitoes.
